subject: Marketplace private offer unit price mapping - AWS/GCP/Azure PO qualification
snippet: Post-call recap + unit price mapping for AWS/GCP marketplace private offers; next steps: confirm monthly token volume and target $/1M tokens.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap: Marketplace private offer pricing (post-demo)

Hi Alan / Kelsey —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and the ask from our side so we can put together an AWS/GCP private offer mapping along with target unit prices:

What we heard:
- Target use: customer-facing chat and search augmentation across web + mobile.
- Expected peak qps: ~80 concurrent users for initial roll-out, expected to grow.
- Current estimate: 150M tokens/month (prompt + generated tokens combined) for year 1; possible ramp to 600M within 12 months if successful.
- Procurement prefers to buy via marketplace private offer if pricing + terms align.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Monthly committed token range you want us to map to private offer SKUs (e.g., 100M, 250M, 1B).
2) Historical monthly spend range you are budgeting for LLM infra (ballpark $/month).
3) Any platform preference (AWS Marketplace private offer first, or should we include GCP/Azure PO mapping in the same doc?).

What we'll provide by EOD Tue: a simple unit price mapping spreadsheet that shows:
- Redwood public API list price equivalence ($/1M tokens)
- Marketplace unit price target (taking marketplace fees and private offer margins into account)
- Example PO line items for AWS/GCP/Azure (how many units to purchase for a given committed volume)

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (draft unit mapping) and AWS_private_offer_terms.pdf (standard PO template) — see attached.

Next steps:
- Alan/Kelsey: confirm committed ranges and preferred marketplace by EOD Tue.
- Marissa/Mateo: we’ll produce a private offer mapping + suggested $/1M token tiers and a short mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifications from procurement / product: 

- The 150M/mo number is our conservative forecast for initial prod (we may run some pilots at ~50M for specific markets). If pilots go well, plan to hit ~500–600M within 9–12 months.
- Budget: for year 1 we have a target range of $6k–$12k/month for LLM infra during pilot; senior leadership will revisit if the metrics justify expansion.
- Marketplace preference: AWS private offer preferred (we have procurement already in AWS Marketplace). If you can provide equivalent mapping for GCP that’s helpful but lower priority.

One ask on unit economics: can you show a target net unit price that maps to about $X per 1M tokens that fits within our budget at the pilot and at the 500M scale? For example, if we buy a 250M commitment, what is the target $/1M after marketplace fees and any reseller margins?

Happy to hop back on a quick 20-minute call if that helps.

—Alan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Marketplace private offer pricing (post-demo)

Alan — thanks, noted. Attached is an updated unit price mapping with three commitment tiers and example PO line items for AWS Marketplace private offers. Key assumptions and example math below so procurement can validate: 

Assumptions:
- Redwood public API reference list price: $8.00 / 1M tokens (example for the model profile used in demo).
- Marketplace listing fees / AWS take (estimated combined reseller+junction fees): ~12% of gross. Private offers typically add a 5–15% negotiated delta depending on volume.
- We assume Redwood Discount to partner/legal minimum + private offer pass-throughs; final net to customer = list_price * (1 - redwood_discount) * (1 + marketplace_markup).

Example tier mapping (see attached spreadsheet for full line items):
- Pilot tier (50M/mo): suggested private-offer unit price = $60 / 1M tokens (this maps to ~$3k/mo at 50M) — used to keep pilot spend within procurement's stated $6k–$12k/month when combined with prod infra and other costs.
- Mid tier (250M/mo): suggested private-offer unit price = $16 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost ~$4k for 250M? (note: verify math below).
- Growth tier (1B/mo): suggested private-offer unit price = $6 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost ~$6k for 1B (example).

Detailed math example (250M tier):
- Public list equivalence: $8.00 / 1M
- Applied Redwood committed discount (example): 40% -> net to Redwood = $4.80 / 1M
- Marketplace markup (AWS private offer + marketplace fees): +10% -> customer-facing unit = $5.28 / 1M
- Rounding / contract simplification -> propose listing private-offer unit at $5.50 / 1M in the PO to simplify invoicing.

Why these matter: procurement needs a straightforward per-1M unit price in the PO. For AWS private offers we typically map committed units to a SKU (e.g., "redwood-1m-tokens-250m") with a unit price that makes billing and consumption simple.

Action items (mutual):
- BrightCart: confirm which tier(s) you want quoted (50M / 250M / 1B) and the target pilot monthly budget ceiling.
- Redwood: Marissa/Aditya will produce a finalized AWS private offer PDF for procurement + a short mutual action plan. We'll also attach a GCP mapping as an appendix.

Notes on accuracy: the spreadsheet includes the exact per-1M math and alternative scenarios if AWS fees differ. If procurement can share the AWS Marketplace fee % they expect (sometimes varies by reseller), we’ll tighten the numbers.

Attachments updated: pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (tab: AWS_PO_mapping).

Proposed next step: 20-min sync Wed 10/7 at 11:00 AM PT to align on tier selection and procurement requirements.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your confirmation.

Marissa
